claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation with your child or children. 

**How old is/are the child or children you're claiming for?** 

The age of the child is the key starting point. Please tell me:
- The age(s) of the child/children you want to claim Child Benefit for
- The name(s) of the child/children so I can track their eligibility properly

Once I know this, I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! Perfect - let me note down that you have **Alex, who is 8 years old**. Since Alex is under 16 years old, they automatically qualify on the age requirement.

Now let me navigate through the next part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check on Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not working at all?**

(This is typically not an issue for 8-year-olds, but I need to confirm for the eligibility check)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense - Alex is 8 years old, so definitely not working. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask about Alex's benefits situation:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, for an 8-year-old this would be unusual, but I need to confirm)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good - now let me check Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(For an 8-year-old, the answer should be no, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility check)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - they're only 8 years old, still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in primary school and not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (with specific conditions like working, looking for work, sufficient resources, studying, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (in certain qualifying countries)

Based on your earlier mention that Alex "lives with me here in the UK," I'm assuming you normally live in the UK - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - I normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the straightforward residency requirement met. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. This means:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** (which you already mentioned - Alex lives with you)
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement**

From what you've told me, it sounds like you live with Alex and provide for them - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me and I provide for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That clearly establishes your responsibility for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is there anyone else claiming or likely to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent (if separated/divorced)
- A grandparent or other relative
- Anyone else

Or are you the only person who would be claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the only person claiming for Alex. Nobody else is getting Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the sole claimant for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check where Alex is living:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **Living at home with you normally** (the typical situation)
- **In hospital** (long-term stay)
- **In local authority care**
- **Fostered with another family**

Based on what you've told me, I'm assuming Alex lives at home with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives at home with you. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final check. Now I need to confirm:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- You're paying for Alex's housing and upkeep yourself, and
- The local council is not providing financial support for Alex's care or accommodation

Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care or accommodation. I'm providing everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me now provide you with the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome formally:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **EXCELLENT NEWS - YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT!**

### Summary for Alex:
**✅ ELIGIBLE**

---

### Why You're Eligible:

You and Alex meet all the requirements for Child Benefit:

1. ✅ **Age requirement**: Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
2. ✅ **Work requirement**: Alex is not working full-time
3. ✅ **Benefits requirement**: Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
4. ✅ **Apprenticeship requirement**: Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
5. ✅ **Residency requirement**: You normally live in the UK
6. ✅ **Responsibility requirement**: You live with Alex and provide for them
7. ✅ **Sole claimant**: You're the only person claiming for Alex
8. ✅ **Living arrangement**: Alex lives at home with you
9. ✅ **Council support**: The council is not paying towards Alex's care

---

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Gather required documents**:
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address (council tax bill, utility bill, etc.)

3. **Important note about the High Income Child Benefit Charge**:
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge

4. **Payment schedule**:
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits, you may be able to get weekly payments

### Useful Links:
- How to claim: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- Eligibility information: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

**Congratulations! You're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.** If you have any other questions or need clarification on the application process, feel free to ask!

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
